f: According to Ibn ʿĀbidīn, what spiritual qualities distinguish the Awliyāʾ of Allah?
b: Allah purified them from worldly impurities, immersed them in the realities of Tawḥīd and divine transcendence, unveiled to them the mysteries of His Names and Attributes, and made their hearts receptacles for His divine manifestations (tajalliyāt).

f: According to Ibn ʿĀbidīn, what benefit do the Awliyāʾ bring to Allah's creation?
b: Allah shows mercy to His servants through them, conceals some of them from public recognition, and grants spiritual benefit through their existence.

f: According to Ibn ʿĀbidīn in Ijābat al-Ghawth, what is a Quṭb (قَطْب) in Sufi terminology?
b: The Quṭb is the hidden spiritual khalīfah and the master of the people of his age (sayyid ahl zamānih). He is called the "Quṭb" because all spiritual stations (maqāmāt) and states (aḥwāl) revolve around him, just as a millstone revolves around its central axle (quṭb al-raḥā).

f: Why is the supreme Sufi saint called the Quṭb according to Ibn ʿĀbidīn?
b: Because all spiritual stations and states revolve around him, just as a millstone revolves around its central pivot (quṭb al-raḥā).

f: How does Ibn al-Fāriḍ (as quoted by Ibn ʿĀbidīn from al-Qāshānī) define the Quṭb?
b: The Quṭb is the most perfect human being (akmal al-nās), firmly established in the station of singularity (maqām al-fardiyyah), around whom the affairs of creation revolve.

f: According to Ibn ʿĀbidīn, what are the two kinds of Quṭb mentioned by al-Qāshānī?
b: (1) A Quṭb governing the created world ('ālam al-shahādah), who is succeeded upon death by the most perfect of the Abdāl. (2) The supreme Quṭb governing both the unseen ('ālam al-ghayb) and the visible world, who has no successor from the Abdāl and is called the Quṭb of all Quṭbs (Quṭb al-Aqṭāb).

f: According to Ibn ʿĀbidīn, who succeeds the ordinary Quṭb after his death?
b: The nearest and most perfect of the Abdāl succeeds him.

f: According to Ibn ʿĀbidīn, what is Quṭb al-Aqṭāb (قُطْبُ الْأَقْطَابِ)?
b: The supreme Quṭb who governs both the unseen and visible worlds, has no successor from the Abdāl, is unmatched among all Quṭbs, and is identified with the Muḥammadan Spirit (al-rūḥ al-muṣṭafawiyyah).

f: According to Ibn ʿĀbidīn, what is meant by the Muḥammadan Spirit (الرُّوحُ الْمُصْطَفَوِيَّةُ)?
b: He identifies it with Quṭb al-Aqṭāb, the supreme spiritual pole over all creation, citing the famous narration "Were it not for you, I would not have created the heavens."

f: According to the editor's note in Ijābat al-Ghawth, how do some Sufis describe the succession of spiritual ranks leading to the Quṭb?
b: One of the four Awtād may be elevated to the rank of one of the two Imāms, and then become the Quṭb.

f: According to the editor of Ijābat al-Ghawth, what is the scholarly status of the narration "Were it not for you (Lawlāk), I would not have created the heavens"?
b: The wording is regarded as weak by some scholars, although the editor argues that its meaning is supported by other narrations concerning the virtue of the Prophet ﷺ.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī (as quoted by Ibn ʿĀbidīn in Ijābat al-Ghawth), how is the term Quṭb (قَطْب) used in both its broad and technical senses?
b: Broadly, any person around whom a particular spiritual station (maqām) revolves and who is unique in that station during his time may be called a Quṭb. Technically, when the term "Quṭb" is used without qualification, it refers to only one individual: the supreme spiritual pole (al-Ghawth) of the age.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, can someone other than the supreme spiritual pole be called a Quṭb?
b: Yes. A person who uniquely embodies a particular spiritual station or who is the central figure of a city, group, or spiritual community may be called the Quṭb of that station, city, or group. However, the unqualified title "the Quṭb" refers only to the single supreme Quṭb (al-Ghawth).

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, who is al-Ghawth (الْغَوْث)?
b: Al-Ghawth is the one supreme Quṭb of every age. When the title "Quṭb" is used absolutely without qualification, it refers to him, and he is the spiritual leader (sayyid) of the people of his time.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, what are the two forms of leadership that the supreme Quṭb may possess?
b: He may possess both outward political leadership (al-khilāfah al-ẓāhirah) and inward spiritual leadership (al-khilāfah al-bāṭinah), or he may possess only the inward spiritual leadership.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, which figures combined both the outward and inward caliphate?
b: He states that Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib combined both the outward and inward caliphate.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, do most Quṭbs possess outward political authority?
b: No. He states that most Quṭbs possess only the inward spiritual caliphate (al-khilāfah al-bāṭinah), not outward political rule.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, what is the difference between a qualified Quṭb (e.g. Quṭb of a city or station) and the absolute Quṭb?
b: A qualified Quṭb is the central figure of a specific station, city, or community, whereas the absolute Quṭb (al-Ghawth) is the unique supreme spiritual pole of the entire age.

f: According to Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī (as quoted in Ijābat al-Ghawth), why are the Rijāl al-Ghayb (Men of the Unseen) called by that name?
b: They are called the Rijāl al-Ghayb because most people do not know them or recognize them. Their leader is the Quṭb al-Ghawth al-Fard (the unique supreme spiritual pole).

f: According to Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī, how does the Quṭb al-Ghawth relate to the world?
b: Allah causes him to revolve through the four regions (arkān) of the world just as the celestial sphere revolves in the heavens. Through him, the well-being (ṣalāḥ) of the world is maintained.

f: According to Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī, who recognizes the Quṭb al-Ghawth?
b: Allah conceals his reality from both the elite and the common people. The Quṭb may appear as a scholar or an ignorant person, intelligent or simple, devoted or seemingly negligent, near or far, easy-going or austere.

f: According to Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī, what analogy describes the Quṭb's relationship to the saints (awliyāʾ)?
b: The Quṭb is to the awliyāʾ like the center point of a circle: just as the circle revolves around its center, the affairs of the saints revolve around the Quṭb.

f: According to Mullā ʿAlī al-Qārī (as quoted in Ijābat al-Ghawth), who was likely the Quṭb of the Abdāl during his lifetime?
b: Mullā ʿAlī al-Qārī says that, in his opinion, Uways al-Qaranī was the Quṭb of the Abdāl in his time.

f: According to the Sufi opinion quoted by Aḥmad al-Manīnī, who became the first Quṭb after the Prophet ﷺ?
b: The opinion quoted states that Fāṭimah al-Zahrāʾ became the first Quṭb after the Prophet ﷺ, although the commentator notes he found no earlier authority for this claim.

f: According to Aḥmad al-Manīnī, who became the Quṭb after the era of the Companions?
b: He states that after the era of the Companions, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ became the Quṭb.

f: According to Ijābat al-Ghawth, who succeeds the Quṭb after his death?
b: One of the two Imāms succeeds him as Quṭb.

f: According to Ijābat al-Ghawth, what are the roles of the two Imāms who assist the Quṭb?
b: They function like two ministers. One is primarily concerned with the world of Malakūt (the unseen spiritual realm), while the other is concerned with the world of Mulk (the visible created world).

f: According to Ijābat al-Ghawth, which of the Quṭb's two Imāms has the higher rank?
b: The Imām whose attention is directed toward the world of Malakūt is considered higher in rank than the one whose attention is directed toward the world of Mulk.

f: According to Ijābat al-Ghawth, what is the linguistic origin of the term Abdāl (الْأَبْدَالِ)?
b: Abdāl is the plural of Badal (بَدَلٌ).

f: According to Ijābat al-Ghawth, why are the saints called the Abdāl?
b: Three explanations are given: (1) whenever one dies, Allah replaces him with another; (2) they replaced their blameworthy character traits with praiseworthy ones through spiritual discipline; (3) they serve as successors to the Prophets.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī (as quoted in Ijābat al-Ghawth), what distinguishes a Badal when he leaves a place?
b: When a Badal departs from a place, he knowingly leaves behind a spiritual reality (ḥaqīqah rūḥāniyyah). If the people strongly long for him, that spiritual reality may become manifest to them, speak with them, and receive their speech, even though the Badal himself is physically absent.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, how does the phenomenon of leaving behind a spiritual presence differ between a Badal and other saints?
b: Other saints may also leave behind a spiritual presence, but the Badal consciously knows that he has left it behind, whereas other saints generally do not.

f: According to al-Qāshānī (as quoted in Ijābat al-Ghawth), who are the Abdāl?
b: The Abdāl are a group of people characterized by divine love (maḥabbah), spiritual unveiling (kashf), witnessing (mushāhadah), and presence (ḥuḍūr). They call people to tawḥīd and submission to Allah.

f: According to al-Qāshānī, what role do the Abdāl play in the world?
b: Through their existence, Allah shows mercy to people and lands, and through them He averts trials, corruption, punishment, and calamities from creation.

f: According to the ḥadīth cited by al-Qāshānī, what qualities characterize the true Abdāl?
b: They are people whose greatest concern and delight are the remembrance of Allah. Allah loves them and they love Him, the veil between them and Him is lifted, they remain mindful when others are heedless, and their speech resembles the speech of the Prophets.

f: According to al-Qāshānī, how many Abdāl are there at any given time?
b: There are always forty Abdāl.

f: According to al-Qāshānī, how are the spiritual ranks of the Abdāl arranged?
b: Their lowest rank corresponds to the highest rank of the righteous (ṣāliḥūn), while their highest rank is immediately below the rank of the Quṭb.

f: According to al-Qāshānī, how is the number of the Abdāl preserved?
b: Whenever one of the forty Abdāl dies, Allah replaces him with someone from the rank below him. This promotion continues downward until a righteous person enters the lowest rank of the Abdāl, so that their number always remains forty until the approach of the Last Day.

f: According to al-Qāshānī, what happens to the Abdāl near the end of time?
b: Their number remains complete until the coming of the Hour, when they all pass away, as mentioned in the reports cited by the author.

f: According to Abū al-Dardāʾ (as quoted by al-Ghazālī in Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn), who are the Abdāl?
b: The Abdāl are the successors (khulafāʾ) of the Prophets and the spiritual pillars (awtād) of the earth. After prophethood ended, Allah established them within the Ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ.

f: According to Abū al-Dardāʾ, by what qualities do the Abdāl surpass others?
b: They do not surpass people through abundant fasting, prayer, or outward appearance, but through sincere waraʿ (scrupulous piety), pure intention, sound hearts toward all Muslims, sincere advice (naṣīḥah) for them seeking Allah's pleasure, steadfast patience, and humility without humiliation.

f: According to the narration of Abū al-Dardāʾ quoted by al-Ghazālī in Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn, how many Abdāl are there and what is the spiritual state of thirty of them?
b: The Abdāl are forty ṣiddīqūn (truthful saints). Thirty of them have hearts possessing a certainty like that of Prophet Ibrāhīm (ʿalayhi al-salām). No one of them dies until Allah has raised another to succeed him.

f: According to the narration of Abū al-Dardāʾ quoted in Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn, what qualities distinguish the Abdāl?
b: They do not curse, harm, belittle, oppress, envy, or covet the world. They are the best of people in goodness, the gentlest in character, the most generous, marked by generosity, cheerfulness, and soundness of heart. They remain constant in their spiritual state, their hearts ascend to Allah in longing, and they hasten toward good deeds.

f: According to Abū al-Dardāʾ, what Qur'ānic verse describes the Abdāl?
b: He cites Allah's statement: "Those are the party of Allah. Indeed, the party of Allah are the successful." (Qur'an 58:22).

f: According to the narration of Abū al-Dardāʾ, what is the path to attaining the qualities of the Abdāl?
b: One must hate attachment to the worldly life. The more one hates the world, the more one loves the Hereafter; the more one loves the Hereafter, the more one renounces the world and recognizes what truly benefits him. If Allah sees sincerity in this pursuit, He grants right guidance and protects him.

f: Which Qur'ānic verse does Abū al-Dardāʾ cite regarding those who attain the qualities of the Abdāl?
b: He cites Allah's statement: "Indeed, Allah is with those who have taqwā and those who are people of excellence (muḥsinūn)." (Qur'an 16:128).

f: What conclusion did Yaḥyā ibn Kathīr draw after reflecting on the qualities of the Abdāl?
b: He said: "We reflected upon this and found that those who delight in anything have found no delight comparable to the love of Allah and seeking His pleasure."

f: According to the account related by Ibn ʿArabī in Ḥilyat al-Abdāl, what four qualities make a person one of the Abdāl?
b: The four qualities are: silence (ṣamt), seclusion (ʿuzlah), hunger (jūʿ), and night vigil (sahar), as mentioned by Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī in Qūt al-Qulūb.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī's account in Ḥilyat al-Abdāl, who was the saint that explained how one becomes one of the Abdāl?
b: Ibn ʿArabī identifies him as one of the Abdāl named Muʿādh ibn Ashras.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī's Ḥilyat al-Abdāl, what are the four pillars of the path leading to the rank of the Abdāl?
b: The four pillars are silence (ṣamt), seclusion (ʿuzlah), hunger (jūʿ), and night vigil (sahar). Whoever has no firm footing in these is considered far from the path to Allah.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, what poem summarizes the four pillars of attaining the rank of the Abdāl?
b: Ibn ʿArabī concludes Ḥilyat al-Abdāl with verses stating that the foundations of sainthood are divided into four pillars: silence, continual seclusion, hunger, and noble night vigil; through these one attains the station and companionship of the Abdāl.

f: According to Ibn ʿĀbidīn, what is the linguistic meaning of Awtād?
b: Awtād is the plural of watad ("peg" or "stake"), a word that may be pronounced with either kasrah or fatḥah on the wāw according to the language scholars.

f: How does Ibn ʿArabī explain why certain saints are called the Awtād (Pegs)?
b: Ibn ʿArabī says they may be referred to as "mountains," citing Allah's words: "Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs?" (Qur'an 78:6–7). Just as mountains stabilize the earth, the Awtād spiritually stabilize the world.

f: According to al-Manīnī quoting al-Manāwī, how many Awtād exist at any given time?
b: There are always four Awtād in every age; their number neither increases nor decreases.

f: According to al-Manīnī quoting al-Manāwī, what are the cosmic functions of the four Awtād?
b: One preserves the East, another the West, another the South, and another the North by Allah's permission.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, what is the relationship between the four Awtād and the Kaʿbah?
b: Each of the four Awtād is assigned one of the four corners (arkān) of the Kaʿbah.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, which prophets correspond to the first three Awtād and the corners of the Kaʿbah?
b: The Awtād are assigned as follows: the saint upon the heart of Ādam has the Syrian (Shāmī) corner; the one upon the heart of Ibrāhīm has the Iraqi corner; and the one upon the heart of ʿĪsā has the Yemeni corner.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, which prophet's heart corresponds to the fourth of the Awtād, and which corner of the Kaʿbah is assigned to him?
b: The fourth Watad is upon the heart of Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ and is assigned the corner of the Black Stone (Rukn al-Ḥajar al-Aswad).

f: According to Ibn ʿĀbidīn, what is the plural of Najīb, and what alternative plural is sometimes used?
b: The regular plural is Nujabāʾ, while Anjāb is also used (though non-standard) for stylistic correspondence with plurals such as Abdāl and Aqṭāb.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, how many Nujabāʾ exist in every age?
b: There are always eight Nujabāʾ in every age; their number neither increases nor decreases.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, what special knowledge distinguishes the Nujabāʾ?
b: They possess knowledge of the eight divine attributes (the seven well-known attributes plus perception as the eighth), their station is the Kursī, and they have unveiled knowledge of the movements of the heavenly bodies through spiritual unveiling (kashf), not through ordinary astronomical methods.

f: What is the linguistic meaning of Naqīb according to al-Ṣiḥāḥ, as quoted by Ibn ʿĀbidīn?
b: A Naqīb is a leader (ʿarīf), the representative, witness, and guarantor of his people.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, what distinguishes the Nuqabāʾ from the Nujabāʾ regarding knowledge of the heavens?
b: The Nuqabāʾ possess knowledge of the ninth heaven (the outermost sphere), whereas the Nujabāʾ possess knowledge of the eight heavens beneath it.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, how many Nuqabāʾ exist in every age, and why is this number significant?
b: There are always twelve Nuqabāʾ, corresponding to the twelve zodiacal constellations (burūj).

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, what knowledge does each Naqīb possess?
b: Each Naqīb knows the special properties of one zodiacal constellation, the divine secrets and effects placed within it, and the movements of both the fixed stars and the wandering planets.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, what spiritual knowledge has Allah entrusted to the Nuqabāʾ?
b: Allah has entrusted them with knowledge of the revealed sacred laws (sharāʾiʿ), insight into the hidden realities and defects of souls, awareness of their deception and cunning, and such knowledge of Iblīs that they know things about him which he does not know about himself.

f: Besides the Quṭb, Abdāl, Awtād, Nujabāʾ, and Nuqabāʾ, what additional class of saints does Ibn ʿArabī mention?
b: He mentions a class called the Afrād ("the Solitaries").

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, what are the heavenly counterparts of the Afrād?
b: Their counterparts among the angels are the al-Arwāḥ al-Muhayyamah (the enraptured spirits), who are also called the Karūbiyyūn (Cherubic angels).

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī, what characterizes the spiritual state of the Afrād?
b: They are wholly absorbed in the Divine Presence, know none but Allah, witness only what they know of Him, possess no independent knowledge from themselves, and occupy a station between ṣiddīqiyyah (perfect truthfulness) and prophethood.

f: According to the report cited by Ibrāhīm al-Laqqānī from Ibn al-Tilimsānī's commentary on al-Shifāʾ, what are the numbers of the various ranks of saints?
b: The Nuqabāʾ are 300, the Nujabāʾ are 70, the Abdāl are 40, the Akhyār are 7, the ʿUmad (also called the Awtād) are 4, and the Ghawth is 1.

f: According to al-Burhān al-Laqqānī in ʿUmdat al-Murīd (quoting Ibn al-Tilimsānī from al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī), what are the numbers and dwelling places of the various ranks of the awliyāʾ?
b: The Nuqabāʾ are 300 and dwell in the Maghrib (West); the Nujabāʾ are 70 and dwell in Egypt; the Abdāl are 40 and dwell in al-Shām (Greater Syria); the Akhyār are 7 and travel throughout the earth; the ʿUmad (also called the Awtād) are 4 and reside in the corners of the earth; and the Ghawth is 1 and resides in Makkah.

f: According to al-Burhān al-Laqqānī's citation, how do the different ranks of the awliyāʾ intercede when a need affecting the general public arises?
b: The Nuqabāʾ first supplicate, followed in order by the Nujabāʾ, Abdāl, Akhyār, and ʿUmad (Awtād). If none of their supplications are answered, the Ghawth supplicates, and his prayer is not left unanswered.

f: According to Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī, how many Nuqabāʾ, Nujabāʾ, Abdāl, Akhyār, ʿUmad, and Ghawth are there?
b: Dhū al-Nūn states that there are 300 Nuqabāʾ, 70 Nujabāʾ, 40 Abdāl, 7 Akhyār, 4 ʿUmad, and 1 Ghawth.

f: According to the report narrated from al-Khiḍr, what did the earth say after the passing of the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, and how did Allah respond?
b: After the Prophet ﷺ passed away, the earth wept and said: "My Lord, no prophet will walk upon me until the Day of Resurrection." Allah replied that He would place upon the earth members of the Prophet's ﷺ community whose hearts resemble the hearts of the prophets and would never leave the earth without them until the Day of Resurrection.

f: According to the report narrated from al-Khiḍr, what are the numbers of the various spiritual ranks that Allah maintains on earth?
b: The report states that there are 300 Awliyāʾ, 70 Nujabāʾ, 40 Awtād, 10 Nuqabāʾ, 7 ʿUrafāʾ, 3 Mukhtārūn (Chosen Ones), and 1 Ghawth.

f: According to the report narrated from al-Khiḍr, how are the spiritual ranks replenished when the Ghawth or another member of the hierarchy dies?
b: When one of the three Mukhtārūn dies, the Ghawth takes his place; one of the seven ʿUrafāʾ becomes the new Ghawth; one of the ten Nuqabāʾ becomes one of the seven; one of the forty Awtād becomes one of the ten; one of the seventy Nujabāʾ becomes one of the forty; one of the three hundred Awliyāʾ becomes one of the seventy; and one of the ordinary believers is raised to become one of the three hundred Awliyāʾ. This process continues until the Trumpet is blown on the Day of Resurrection.

f: How does Ibn ʿĀbidīn reconcile the differing reports concerning the numbers of the various ranks of the awliyāʾ?
b: He suggests that reports mentioning larger numbers count all members of a rank, whereas reports mentioning smaller numbers refer only to the chiefs or leaders of that rank, while the remaining members still belong to it. He considers this explanation preferable to saying that the stated numbers carry no significance.

f: According to the narrations cited by Ibn ʿĀbidīn, what did the Prophet ﷺ say about reviling the people of al-Shām?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not revile the people of al-Shām, for among them are the Abdāl."

f: What wording of the hadith about the people of al-Shām adds a prohibition against generalizing blame?
b: One narration states: "Do not generalize (your condemnation), for among them are the Abdāl."

f: According to one narration cited by Ibn ʿĀbidīn, where are the Abdāl and the Nujabāʾ located?
b: The narration states: "The Abdāl are in al-Shām, and the Nujabāʾ are in Kūfah."

f: According to another narration cited by Ibn ʿĀbidīn, where are the Awtād and the Abdāl located?
b: The narration states: "The Awtād are among the people of Kūfah, and the Abdāl are among the people of al-Shām."

f: According to another narration cited by Ibn ʿĀbidīn, where are the Nujabāʾ, Akhyār, Quṭb, and Abdāl located?
b: The narration states: "The Nujabāʾ are in Egypt, the Akhyār are among the people of Iraq, the Quṭb is in Yemen, and the Abdāl are in al-Shām, and they are few."

f: How does Ibn ʿĀbidīn reconcile the reports that place the Nujabāʾ in both Kūfah and Egypt?
b: He explains that the reports indicate that the Nujabāʾ are not restricted to one location. At one time they may be in Kūfah, and at another time in Egypt, so there is no contradiction between the narrations.

f: According to the narration cited from ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), what did the Prophet ﷺ say about the people of Syria (al-Shām) because of the presence of the Abdāl?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not revile the people of al-Shām, for among them are the Abdāl." Other narrations include: "Do not wrong them, for among them are the Abdāl."

f: According to the narrations cited from ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), where are the Abdāl, Nujabāʾ, Awtād, Quṭb, and Akhyār located?
b: The narrations state: The Abdāl are in al-Shām; the Nujabāʾ are in Kūfah (and another narration says Egypt); the Awtād are among the people of Kūfah; the Akhyār are from Iraq; and the Quṭb is in Yemen.

f: How does the author reconcile the reports that place the Nujabāʾ in Kūfah with those that place them in Egypt?
b: He explains that there is no contradiction. The Nujabāʾ are not permanently restricted to one place; at one time they may be in Kūfah, and at another time in Egypt.

f: According to the narration reported by Imam Aḥmad from ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), how many Abdāl are there in al-Shām, and what are their functions?
b: There are forty Abdāl in al-Shām. Through them rain is sent, victory over enemies is granted, and punishment is averted from the people of al-Shām.

f: How do al-Shihāb al-Manīnī and Mullā ʿAlī al-Qārī explain the mention of the people of al-Shām specifically receiving victory through the Abdāl?
b: They explain that although other narrations mention their benefit generally, the people of al-Shām are singled out because those living nearest to the Abdāl benefit from their support most directly, without excluding benefit to others.

f: According to the narration in Kitāb al-Awliyāʾ attributed to Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, what qualities distinguish the Abdāl?
b: They are not extremists (mutanaṭṭiʿūn), innovators (mubtadiʿūn), or excessively pedantic (mutaʿammiqūn). They attained their rank not through abundant prayer, fasting, or charity, but through generosity of soul, purity of heart, and sincere counsel toward their leaders.

f: According to the narration from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), how many Abdāl are there, where are they located, and what happens when one dies?
b: There are forty Abdāl: twenty-two in al-Shām and eighteen in Iraq. Whenever one dies, Allah replaces him with another, and when they all pass away, the Hour will come.

f: According to the narration cited from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), how many male and female Abdāl are there?
b: There are forty male Abdāl and forty female Abdāl. Whenever a man dies, Allah replaces him with another man, and whenever a woman dies, Allah replaces her with another woman.

f: According to the narration reported by Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), why do the Abdāl of the Prophet's ﷺ ummah enter Paradise?
b: They do not enter Paradise because of abundant prayer or fasting, but because of the soundness of their hearts (salāmat ṣudūrihim), generosity of spirit (sakhāwat anfusihim), and sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) for the Muslims.

f: According to the narration with a good chain from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), what permanent group will always remain on earth, and what blessings come through them?
b: The earth will never be without forty men like the Friend of the Most Merciful (Prophet Ibrāhīm). Through them rain is sent and victory is granted. Whenever one of them dies, Allah replaces him with another.

f: Who did Qatādah identify as being among the forty men described in the narration stating that the earth will never be without forty men like Prophet Ibrāhīm?
b: Qatādah said: "We have no doubt that al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī is one of them."

f: According to the statement attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them), how many righteous people has Allah always maintained on earth since the time of Prophet Nūḥ, and what is their role?
b: The earth has never been without seven people since the time of Prophet Nūḥ. Through them Allah protects the people of the earth.

f: According to the ḥadīth narrated from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them), how many of the best people and how many Abdāl exist in every generation?
b: In every generation there are five hundred of the best people (khiyār) and forty Abdāl. Their numbers never decrease, because whenever one dies, Allah replaces him.

f: According to the ḥadīth narrated from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them), how are vacancies among the five hundred and the forty Abdāl filled?
b: Whenever one of the five hundred dies, Allah replaces him with another from among the people, and whenever one of the forty Abdāl dies, one from the five hundred is elevated to take his place.

f: According to the ḥadīth narrated from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them), what qualities characterize the Abdāl and the best people of the ummah?
b: They forgive those who wrong them, do good to those who mistreat them, and share with others from what Allah has given them.

f: According to the narration from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them), what did the Prophet ﷺ say about the righteous of every generation of his ummah?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Every generation of my ummah has forerunners (sābiqūn)."

f: According to the narration from Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), how are the righteous ranks of people arranged by number and by whose hearts they resemble?
b: They are arranged as follows: 300 whose hearts are like Adam's عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ; 40 whose hearts are like Ibrāhīm's; 5 whose hearts are like Jibrīl's; 3 whose hearts are like Mīkāʾīl's; and 1 whose heart is like Isrāfīl's.

f: According to the narration from Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), how are the higher spiritual ranks replenished when one of their members dies?
b: When the one dies, one of the three replaces him; when one of the three dies, one of the five replaces him; when one of the five dies, one of the forty replaces him; when one of the forty dies, one of the three hundred replaces him; and when one of the three hundred dies, Allah replaces him from the general body of the people.

f: According to the narration from Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), what blessings come through these righteous people?
b: Through them Allah gives life and causes death, brings forth vegetation, and repels afflictions.

f: According to Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), how do these righteous people become a means for Allah's blessings upon creation?
b: They supplicate for the increase of nations, so Allah increases them; pray against tyrants, so Allah destroys them; ask for rain, so rain is sent; ask for vegetation, so the earth produces; and pray for protection, so Allah repels various calamities through them.

f: According to the author's explanation, why is no one described as being "upon the heart of" the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ in the narration listing the spiritual ranks?
b: The author explains that the Prophet's ﷺ heart is the noblest, most honored, and most perfect heart in all creation. Compared to it, the hearts of prophets, angels, and saints are like the stars compared to the sun, so no one is explicitly described as being upon his heart in that narration.

f: How does the author reconcile Ibn ʿArabī's statement that one of the Awtād is upon the heart of the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ with the narration that does not mention anyone upon the Prophet's ﷺ heart?
b: He explains that Ibn ʿArabī intended that this person receives divine knowledge through the Muhammadan reality and possesses the highest rank among his peers, not that he is literally identical to the Prophet ﷺ in every respect.

f: According to Ibn ʿArabī's explanation cited by the author, what does it mean for a saint to be "upon the heart" of a prophet or an angel?
b: It means that the saint receives divine knowledge and spiritual unveilings through the heart of that prophet or angel, since divine sciences descend upon hearts, and the saint receives according to that spiritual channel.

f: What did al-Shihāb al-Manīnī report regarding Ibn al-Jawzī's and al-Suyūṭī's positions on the aḥādīth of the Abdāl?
b: Al-Manīnī said that Ibn al-Jawzī criticized the aḥādīth concerning the Abdāl and judged them to be fabricated, but al-Suyūṭī refuted him, stating that the reports concerning the Abdāl are authentic, and even said that they may be regarded as mutawātir in meaning (tawātur maʿnawī), making the existence of the Abdāl a matter established by necessity due to the abundance of reports.

f: How did al-Sakhāwī evaluate the narrations concerning the Abdāl?
b: Al-Sakhāwī stated that the reports about the Abdāl come through numerous chains with varying wordings, but that all of them are individually weak. However, he regarded the strongest of them to be the narration recorded by Imam Aḥmad from ʿAlī (may Allah honor his face): "The Abdāl are in Syria. They are forty men. Whenever one dies, Allah replaces him with another. Through them rain is sent, victory is granted over enemies, and punishment is averted from the people of Syria." He added that its narrators are those of Ṣaḥīḥ collections except for Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, who is trustworthy.

f: What was Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī's assessment of the reports concerning the Abdāl, the Quṭb, and the Ghawth?
b: Ibn Ḥajar stated that several reports exist concerning the Abdāl, some authentic and some not. As for the Quṭb, it is mentioned in some transmitted reports. As for the Ghawth in the well-known Sufi sense, he said that it has not been established by authentic evidence.

f: According to some narrations cited by Ibn Ḥajar, what are two signs of the Abdāl?
b: Some narrations mention that among the signs of the Abdāl are: (1) they do not have children, and (2) they never curse anything.

f: According to the definition cited from al-Qāshānī, what is the difference between the Ghawth and the Quṭb?
b: Everything said about the Ghawth also applies to the Quṭb, except that the Ghawth is the unique saint of the age to whom people actually turn for help in times of need. If people do not seek refuge in his care, he is simply the Quṭb and is not called the Ghawth.

f: How did the author explain Ibn Ḥajar's statement that the Ghawth is not established?
b: The author explains that Ibn Ḥajar meant only that the title Ghawth is not established in authentic Prophetic hadith. Its widespread acceptance among the people of the Sufi path and the abundance of reports about it are, in the author's view, sufficient to affirm its usage.

f: According to Imam al-Yāfiʿī, who is the single individual mentioned in the hierarchy of saints?
b: Imam al-Yāfiʿī said that the single individual referred to is the Quṭb, who is the Ghawth.

f: How did Ibn Ḥajar explain the differing numbers reported for ranks such as the Abdāl, Nuqabāʾ, Nujabāʾ, and Awtād?
b: Ibn Ḥajar suggested that these numbers are terminological designations (iṣṭilāḥāt) referring to different spiritual ranks. Scholars described these ranks using names such as Abdāl, Nuqabāʾ, Nujabāʾ, and Awtād, while different narrations may refer to other classifications. Thus, the apparent differences in numbers can be reconciled.

f: What theological difficulty did Ibn Ḥajar identify in one of the reports about the spiritual hierarchy?
b: He noted that the report would imply that the angels are superior to the prophets, whereas the position of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah is that the prophets are superior to all the angels, except for a minority who held otherwise.

f: What theological difficulty did Ibn Ḥajar identify regarding the relative status of Mīkāʾīl, Jibrīl, and Isrāfīl?
b: The report appears to imply that Mīkāʾīl is superior to Jibrīl, whereas the commonly held view is otherwise. As for Isrāfīl, he is regarded as superior to Mīkāʾīl, while scholars differ over whether Jibrīl or Isrāfīl is superior.

f: What are the two main opinions regarding whether Jibrīl or Isrāfīl is superior?
b: One opinion holds that Jibrīl is superior because he is entrusted with conveying revelation to the prophets and overseeing the mission of prophethood. The other holds that Isrāfīl is superior because the Preserved Tablet is before him, the other angels receive information from it through him, and he is entrusted with the Trumpet awaiting Allah's command to blow it.

f: How did Ibn Ḥajar assess the authenticity of the lengthy report discussing these angelic and saintly ranks?
b: Ibn Ḥajar stated that he did not find the report transmitted by the reliable hadith authorities, although he said that other hadiths support many of its individual meanings.

f: How did Ibn Ḥajar reconcile the different hadiths that mention varying numbers of Abdāl?
b: He suggested that "Abdāl" has more than one usage, as indicated by the differing descriptions and characteristics found in the narrations, or that their number may vary from one era to another, such as forty in one time and thirty in another.

f: How did al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī describe his early upbringing in relation to belief in the Quṭb, Abdāl, and other ranks of awliyāʾ?
b: Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī said that he was raised among members of the Sufi path (the awliyāʾ), so their teachings took root in his heart from childhood. As a result, he firmly believed in the existence of the Quṭb, Abdāl, Nujabāʾ, Nuqabāʾ, and the other spiritual ranks before formally studying the outward Islamic sciences.

f: What was Shaykh Muḥammad al-Juwaynī's position regarding the Quṭb, Abdāl, Nujabāʾ, Nuqabāʾ, and other spiritual ranks when Ibn Ḥajar discussed the matter with him?
b: Shaykh Muḥammad al-Juwaynī denied the existence of the Quṭb, Abdāl, Nujabāʾ, Nuqabāʾ, and the other spiritual ranks mentioned by the Sufis. He declared that they had no reality and that nothing concerning them had been authentically transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ.

f: How did Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī defend the belief in the existence of the Quṭb, Abdāl, and other spiritual ranks when Shaykh Muḥammad al-Juwaynī denied them?
b: Ibn Ḥajar responded that the existence of the Quṭb, Abdāl, and the other spiritual ranks is true because the awliyāʾ of Allah have reported it, and they would not knowingly lie. He also cited Imam al-Yāfiʿī as a scholar who combined both the outward and inward sciences and affirmed these realities.

f: How did Shaykh al-Islām Zakariyyā al-Anṣārī answer when asked whether the Quṭb, Awtād, Nujabāʾ, Abdāl, and the other spiritual ranks mentioned by the Sufis really exist?
b: Shaykh al-Islām Zakariyyā al-Anṣārī answered unequivocally: "Yes, by Allah, my son." He explicitly affirmed the existence of the Quṭb, Awtād, Nujabāʾ, Abdāl, and the other spiritual ranks spoken of by the Sufis.

f: What happened after Shaykh al-Islām Zakariyyā al-Anṣārī learned that Shaykh Muḥammad al-Juwaynī had denied the existence of the Quṭb, Abdāl, and the other spiritual ranks?
b: After Shaykh al-Islām Zakariyyā al-Anṣārī questioned him, Shaykh Muḥammad al-Juwaynī retracted his earlier denial, saying: "O our master, Shaykh al-Islām, I believe in it, affirm it, and have repented." Zakariyyā al-Anṣārī then replied: "That is what I expected from you, O Shaykh Muḥammad."

f: According to the hadith narrated from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, what three qualities make a person one of the Abdāl?
b: According to the hadith narrated from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, a person is among the Abdāl if he possesses three qualities: contentment with Allah's decree (riḍā bi-l-qaḍāʾ), patience in refraining from what Allah has forbidden, and becoming angry for the sake of Allah.

f: According to the narration recorded in Ḥilyat al-Awliyāʾ, what supplication, if recited ten times daily, results in being written among the Abdāl?
b: The narration states that whoever says ten times each day: "O Allah, rectify the Ummah of Muhammad. O Allah, relieve the Ummah of Muhammad. O Allah, have mercy upon the Ummah of Muhammad." will be written among the Abdāl.

f: How did al-Shabrāmallisī explain the meaning of being "written among the Abdāl" in the narration found in Ḥilyat al-Awliyāʾ?
b: Al-Shabrāmallisī explained that being "among the Abdāl" means that the person resembles the Abdāl in their qualities and will be gathered with them on the Day of Resurrection. It does not necessarily mean that he literally becomes one of the fixed number of Abdāl.

f: How did al-Shabrāmallisī reconcile the narration promising that a person will be "written among the Abdāl" with reports stating that the Abdāl do not have children?
b: Al-Shabrāmallisī explained that the narration refers to sharing the Abdāl's virtues and reward, not literally becoming one of the fixed Abdāl. Therefore, there is no contradiction if the person who recites the supplication has many children, even though some reports describe the Abdāl as not having children.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, does the Quṭb (Ghawth) permanently reside in Makkah?
b: Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ said that the Quṭb's body is not permanently confined to Makkah or any other place; rather, it is wherever Allah wills. However, the heart of the Quṭb is constantly circumambulating the Divine Presence, just as people circumambulate the Kaʿbah, never departing from Allah's Presence.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, what is meant by saying that the Quṭb's heart is "circumambulating the Divine Presence"?
b: He explained that the Quṭb continually witnesses Allah in every direction and from every direction, without attributing spatial limitation to Allah. The Quṭb remains constantly turned toward Allah while bearing the spiritual burden of all Divine decrees and assistance that flow to creation.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, why is the Quṭb's head described as nearly splitting apart?
b: Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ said that the Quṭb's head is nearly split apart because of the immense weight of the Divine spiritual influxes (al-wāridāt) that pass through him as he bears the responsibility for the Divine assistance and decrees reaching creation.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, what symbolic relationship exists between the Sacred Precinct (Makkah), the Kaʿbah, and the Quṭb?
b: He explained that the Sacred Precinct (Makkah) corresponds to the Quṭb's body, while the Kaʿbah corresponds to the Quṭb's heart. From the Quṭb, spiritual assistance (imdād) is distributed to creation according to each person's preparedness.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, why do spiritual influxes (imdādāt) descend most abundantly in Makkah?
b: He explained that spiritual influxes descend most abundantly in Makkah because Allah says, "To it are brought the fruits of every thing" (Qur'an 28:57). They especially descend upon pilgrims who come from distant lands in a state of iḥrām after stripping themselves of self-admiration and recognizing their spiritual poverty before Allah.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, what spiritual condition is required for Divine spiritual assistance (imdād) to descend upon a servant?
b: Divine spiritual assistance descends only upon a servant who has become detached from admiring his own good deeds and has attained true spiritual poverty (faqr) before Allah.

f: How did Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ connect the hadith about an accepted Hajj to spiritual rebirth?
b: He explained that the hadith, "Whoever performs Hajj without obscenity or sin returns as on the day his mother gave birth to him," indicates that the pilgrim experiences a new spiritual birth in Makkah, and that even deeds considered good elsewhere may be viewed as deficient in the sanctity of that sacred place.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, can ordinary awliyāʾ fully know the character and spiritual reality of the Quṭb?
b: Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ said that very few awliyāʾ even recognize who the Quṭb is, let alone fully comprehend his spiritual qualities and reality.

f: According to one opinion cited by Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, how does the Quṭb appear to those who see him?
b: One opinion states that the Quṭb is seen only in a form corresponding to the spiritual capacity and preparedness of the observer.

f: What question did the author ask Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ regarding the office of the Quṭb at the end of this passage?
b: The author asked Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ whether the office of the Quṭb has a fixed term of appointment, whether a Quṭb can be removed from office during his lifetime, or whether he leaves the office only through death.

f: According to Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, does the office of Quṭb (Quṭbiyyah) have a fixed term?
b: No. He says the office of Quṭb has no fixed duration. Once a person assumes it, he remains Quṭb until death.

f: Why, according to Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, is the Quṭb not removed from office before death?
b: Because it is not possible for the Quṭb to depart from justice (ʿadl) in a way that would necessitate his removal.

f: What argument does Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ give for the continuity of the Quṭb's office?
b: He argues that branches follow their principles: just as the Prophet ﷺ remained in supreme spiritual leadership throughout his twenty-three-year mission, so too the Quṭb remains in office until death.

f: How long does Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ say the Prophet ﷺ remained in the "great Quṭbiyyah"?
b: Throughout the duration of his prophetic mission, which he states was twenty-three years according to the strongest opinion.

f: Who does Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ identify as the first Quṭb of the Muslim Ummah after the Prophet ﷺ?
b: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, whom he describes as the first of the Quṭbs of this Ummah.

f: According to Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, who continues the succession of Quṭbs after Abū Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ?
b: ʿUmar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, then ʿUthmān, then ʿAlī, followed by successive Quṭbs until the appearance of the Mahdī.

f: According to Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, who is the final Quṭb among the Muhammadan successors?
b: The Mahdī is the last Quṭb among the Muhammadan successors (al-khulafāʾ al-Muḥammadiyyūn).

f: According to Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, who becomes the Quṭb after the Mahdī?
b: Prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus) عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ descends and becomes the Quṭb of his time and Allah's vicegerent (khalīfah) on earth.

f: How long, according to Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, will Prophet ʿĪsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ remain in this office?
b: He will remain in the caliphate for forty years, as reported in the traditions.

f: Why does Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ say the office of Quṭb is extremely burdensome?
b: Because every calamity descending from heaven reaches the Quṭb before it reaches the earth, although Allah grants him strength to bear it.

f: What physical effect does Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ describe as resulting from the Quṭb bearing these burdens?
b: He says the Quṭb constantly suffers severe headaches, as though someone were continually striking his head day and night.

f: Which saint is reported to have remained Quṭb for only forty days?
b: Shaykh Abū al-Najā Sālim is reported to have remained Quṭb for forty days before dying.

f: What alternate report is given regarding Shaykh Abū al-Najā Sālim's period as Quṭb?
b: Another report says he remained Quṭb for only ten days.

f: Which other saint is said to have held the office of Quṭb only briefly?
b: Shaykh Abū Madyan al-Maghribī.

f: According to Sīdī ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, must the Quṭb be from the Ahl al-Bayt?
b: No. He explicitly states that being from the Prophet's ﷺ family is not a condition, because Quṭbiyyah is a Divine gift granted to whomever Allah wills.

f: Why is the Quṭb hidden from most people according to the text?
b: Because of the immense spiritual burdens he bears and the awe and majesty with which Allah has clothed him.

f: Who is generally able to recognize the Quṭb according to the text?
b: Only the spiritual singular ones (al-Afrād) among the saints are generally able to recognize him.

f: According to Imam al-Shaʿrānī's shaykh, can most saints even meet the Quṭb?
b: No. Most saints cannot meet him and do not even know who he is because concealment is one of his defining characteristics.

f: What would happen if the Quṭb appeared before someone who was not spiritually prepared?
b: Such a person would be unable even to raise his head to look at the Quṭb unless he had been specially prepared for that encounter.

f: Which prophetic hadith is cited to illustrate the overwhelming awe inspired by the Quṭb?
b: The hadith in which a man trembled before the Prophet ﷺ, whereupon the Prophet ﷺ said: "Take it easy, for I am only the son of a woman from Quraysh who used to eat dried meat." The author says that if this occurred before the Prophet ﷺ despite his humility, then the Quṭb, as his representative on earth, likewise inspires overwhelming awe.

f: What incident does al-Shaʿrānī relate from Sharaf al-Dīn concerning Shaykh ʿUthmān al-Ḥaṭṭāb and the Quṭb?
b: Al-Shaʿrānī relates that Shaykh ʿUthmān al-Ḥaṭṭāb asked his shaykh, Abū Bakr al-Daqdūsī رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, during the ḥajj to arrange for him to meet the Quṭb in Mecca.

f: How did Shaykh Abū Bakr al-Daqdūsī رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ initially respond when Shaykh ʿUthmān al-Ḥaṭṭāb requested to meet the Quṭb?
b: He warned him, saying: "O ʿUthmān, you cannot bear seeing him."

f: Where did Shaykh Abū Bakr al-Daqdūsī رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ tell Shaykh ʿUthmān al-Ḥaṭṭāb to wait for the Quṭb?
b: He seated him between Zamzam and Maqām Ibrāhīm and instructed him not to leave until the Quṭb arrived.

f: What happened to Shaykh ʿUthmān al-Ḥaṭṭāb while waiting for the Quṭb?
b: His head became so heavy that his beard was forced down between his thighs against his will.

f: What occurred when the Quṭb arrived according to the narrative?
b: The Quṭb sat with Shaykh Abū Bakr al-Daqdūsī رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ and conversed with him for some time.

f: What did the Quṭb say about Shaykh ʿUthmān al-Ḥaṭṭāb?
b: He told Shaykh Abū Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: "Take good care of ʿUthmān, for if he lives, he will become one of Allah's men."

f: Which Qur'anic passages did the Quṭb recite before departing?
b: He recited Sūrat al-Fātiḥah and Sūrat Quraysh (Li-īlāfi Quraysh) before leaving.

f: What did Shaykh Abū Bakr al-Daqdūsī رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ do after accompanying the Quṭb?
b: He returned and repeatedly pressed Shaykh ʿUthmān's neck until he regained the ability to hear and speak.

f: What lesson did Shaykh Abū Bakr al-Daqdūsī رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ draw from Shaykh ʿUthmān's condition?
b: He said: "This is what happened to you merely from hearing his speech; what would have happened had you actually looked upon him?"

f: What practice did Shaykh ʿUthmān al-Ḥaṭṭāb adopt after this encounter?
b: Whenever he met someone and then parted from them, he would recite Sūrat al-Fātiḥah and Sūrat Quraysh, seeking blessing from what he had heard the Quṭb recite.

f: According to Imam al-Yāfiʿī as quoted by al-Shubrī, from whom are the states of the Quṭb concealed?
b: The states of the Quṭb, who is also the Ghawth, are concealed from both the general public and even the spiritual elite out of Allah's protective jealousy (ghayrah) over him.

f: According to Imam al-Yāfiʿī, how does the Quṭb appear to people?
b: He appears as an ordinary person: a scholar like an ignorant man, intelligent like a simpleton, one who leaves things and one who takes them, near yet far, easy yet difficult, secure yet cautious.

f: According to Imam al-Yāfiʿī, whose spiritual states are disclosed to the spiritual elite (al-khāṣṣah)?
b: The spiritual states of the Awtād are disclosed to the spiritual elite.

f: According to Imam al-Yāfiʿī, whose spiritual states are disclosed to both the spiritual elite and the gnostics (al-ʿārifūn)?
b: The spiritual states of the Abdāl are disclosed to both the spiritual elite and the gnostics.

f: According to Imam al-Yāfiʿī, from whom are the spiritual states of the Nujabāʾ and Nuqabāʾ concealed?
b: They are concealed from the general public, although members of these ranks may recognize one another.

f: According to Imam al-Yāfiʿī, whose spiritual state is openly recognized by both the public and the elite?
b: The spiritual state of the righteous (al-ṣāliḥūn) is apparent to both the general public and the spiritual elite.

f: Which Qur'anic verse does Imam al-Yāfiʿī cite after describing the concealment of the saints?
b: He cites: "So that Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed." (Qur'an 8:42).

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ as quoted by al-Shaʿrānī, how does affliction (balāʾ) reach creation through the Quṭb (Ghawth)?
b: Every affliction destined for the people of the earth first descends upon the Quṭb. He receives it with fear and acceptance, then waits to see what Allah manifests in the Preserved Tablet regarding whether it will be erased or confirmed.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, what happens if the affliction is erased (maḥw) after descending upon the Quṭb?
b: If Allah manifests that the affliction has been erased or changed, the Divine decree is carried out and concluded through the Ahl al-Taslīk (the attendants of the Divine Presence), who execute it without realizing that it has been transmitted to them through the Quṭb.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, what happens if the affliction remains confirmed (ithbāt) and is not erased?
b: The Quṭb passes it to the two Imāms closest to him. They bear it and pass it to the four Awtād, who in turn pass it through the remaining spiritual hierarchy until it reaches all those within their circle.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, how does the affliction continue to spread if it is still not lifted?
b: If it is still not removed, it is distributed through the Afrād and other gnostics (ʿārifūn) until it eventually reaches the ordinary believers, through whose endurance Allah ultimately lifts it.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, how can the distribution of spiritual afflictions appear in ordinary believers?
b: A person may suddenly feel unexplained constriction, anxiety, sleeplessness, heedlessness, or prolonged silence without knowing the cause. These states are described as portions of the distributed affliction.

f: According to Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ, why are afflictions distributed among many people rather than borne by one alone?
b: Because if the affliction were not distributed, whoever received it directly would perish in an instant. Allah distributes it among many servants out of His mercy.

f: Which Qur'anic verse does Shaykh ʿAlī al-Khawwāṣ cite as evidence for the distribution of afflictions among people?
b: He cites Qur'an 2:251: "Had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would surely have become corrupted. But Allah is full of bounty to all the worlds."

f: Why does the author transition from discussing the Quṭb to discussing miracles (karāmāt)?
b: Because the extraordinary rank and states of the Quṭb naturally lead into a discussion of karāmāt (saintly miracles) and other supernatural events that Allah manifests through His awliyāʾ.

f: According to Imām al-Qushayrī in al-Risālah, what are the two primary meanings of the word walī?
b: (1) It may be an intensive active participle (faʿīl) meaning one whose obedience to Allah is continuous without interruption by sin. (2) It may be a passive participle (faʿīl meaning mafʿūl), referring to one whom Allah continually protects, guards, and grants success, preventing him from being abandoned to disobedience.

f: According to Imām al-Qushayrī, what characterizes the walī if the word is understood as an intensive active participle?
b: The walī is one whose obedience to Allah is continuous and uninterrupted by disobedience.

f: According to Imām al-Qushayrī, what characterizes the walī if the word is understood as a passive participle?
b: The walī is one whom Allah continuously protects and preserves, withholding abandonment (khidhlān) and perpetually granting divine success (tawfīq) to obey Him.

f: According to Imām al-Qushayrī, what Qur'anic verse supports the idea that a walī is divinely protected?
b: He cites Allah's statement: "And He is the Protector of the righteous." (Qur'an 7:196), indicating that Allah Himself preserves His awliyāʾ.

f: According to the author, what level of protection (ḥifẓ) is required for a walī?
b: A walī must be divinely protected, though not infallible like a prophet. If he falls into an error or sin, Allah inspires him to repent, so such lapses do not invalidate his sainthood.

f: According to Imām al-Qushayrī, does a sin or mistake nullify a person's wilāyah?
b: No. A walī may commit an error or sin, but Allah preserves him by inspiring sincere repentance. Therefore, such lapses do not invalidate his wilāyah.

f: What famous incident involving al-Junayd does Imām al-Qushayrī relate concerning the possibility of a walī committing a sin?
b: When al-Junayd was asked, "Can a knower of Allah (ʿārif) commit adultery?" he remained silent for some time, then recited: "And the command of Allah is a decree already determined." (Qur'an 33:38).

f: According to Imām al-Qushayrī, what qualities characterize a walī during his state of spiritual sobriety (ṣaḥw)?
b: A walī is characterized by truthful fulfillment of Allah's rights, mercy and compassion toward all creation, beautiful character, seeking Allah's goodness for others without being asked, concern for people's salvation, refraining from revenge and hatred, avoiding greed for others' wealth, restraining his tongue from speaking ill, overlooking people's faults, and not becoming anyone's adversary in this world or the next.

f: According to the author, what is the definition of a karāmah (saintly miracle)?
b: A karāmah is the appearance of an event that breaks the normal course of nature at the hands of a person who is outwardly righteous, adheres to the guidance of a prophet, possesses sound belief and righteous deeds, and does not claim prophethood.

f: What distinguishes a karāmah from a muʿjizah (prophetic miracle)?
b: A karāmah occurs through a saint who does not claim prophethood, whereas a muʿjizah is connected with a prophet and serves as proof of his prophethood.

f: What distinguishes a karāmah from istidrāj (gradual divine deception)?
b: A karāmah is accompanied by sound belief and righteous deeds, whereas istidrāj appears at the hands of an openly sinful person despite his corruption.

f: What example does the author give of ihānah (humiliation) through false miracles?
b: He cites Musaylimah al-Kadhdhāb: when he prayed for a blind eye to be healed, the healthy eye became blind; when he spat into a well to sweeten it, it became salty; and when he stroked an orphan's head, the child became bald. These are examples of humiliation rather than miracles.

f: What is muʿūnah (divine assistance), according to the author?
b: Muʿūnah consists of extraordinary events granted to ordinary Muslims to rescue them from hardships and difficulties.

f: According to the author, what are the four primary categories of supernatural events (khawāriq)?
b: They are: (1) Muʿjizah (prophetic miracle), (2) Karāmah (saintly miracle), (3) Ihānah (humiliation of a false claimant), and (4) Muʿūnah (divine assistance for ordinary believers).

f: Which three additional categories of supernatural phenomena do some later scholars add?
b: They add Irhāṣ (pre-prophetic signs before a prophet's mission), Istidrāj (extraordinary occurrences granted to sinful people as a trial), and Siḥr/Shaʿbadhah (magic or illusion performed through specific means).

f: What is irhāṣ according to the author?
b: Irhāṣ refers to extraordinary signs that occur before a prophet publicly claims prophethood, such as stones greeting the Prophet ﷺ or clouds shading him before his mission.

f: What is istidrāj according to the author?
b: Istidrāj is an extraordinary occurrence that appears at the hands of someone openly sinful, in accordance with his claim, as a means of gradual deception and trial, such as what occurred with Pharaoh.

f: What is siḥr or shaʿbadhah according to the author?
b: It refers to extraordinary effects produced through specific causes or techniques, such as handling venomous snakes without apparent harm.

f: According to the author, what two aspects does every supernatural event shown through a gnostic (ʿārif) possess?
b: It is a karāmah with respect to the saint through whom it appears, and simultaneously a muʿjizah with respect to the Prophet ﷺ whose religion that saint follows.

f: Why is every karāmah of a saint also considered evidence for the Prophet ﷺ?
b: Because the saint's wilāyah depends upon his truthful belief in and obedience to the Messenger ﷺ. The appearance of a karāmah therefore confirms the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ whom the saint follows.

f: Could someone who claims independence from the Prophet ﷺ still be a walī who manifests karāmāt?
b: No. Anyone claiming independence from the Prophet ﷺ and refusing to follow him is not a walī, and true karāmāt would not appear through him.

f: From the perspective of the Prophet ﷺ, how are all supernatural events manifested through members of his community regarded?
b: They are all considered manifestations of his prophetic miracle (muʿjizah), whether they occur directly through him or through one of his followers.

f: According to the author, what distinguishes a prophet from a walī regarding miraculous signs?
b: A prophet knows with certainty that he is a prophet, intentionally presents miracles as proof of his mission, and establishes legal authority through them. A walī does not claim prophethood, and his karāmāt are not intended as proofs of prophethood.

f: How did Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī describe the relationship between the miracles of the prophets and the karāmāt of the awliyāʾ?
b: He said that what the prophets received is like a vessel filled with honey from which only a single drop drips. That drop represents everything granted to all the awliyāʾ combined, while the honey remaining in the vessel represents what was granted to the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ.

f: What does Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī's analogy imply about the relationship between prophetic miracles and saintly miracles?
b: It emphasizes the immense superiority of the prophets—especially the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ—over all the awliyāʾ, whose combined karāmāt are likened to only a single drop compared to the prophets' abundance.

f: According to the author, can a karāmah be of the same type as a prophetic miracle (muʿjizah)?
b: Yes. The author states that a karāmah may be of the same type as a prophetic miracle, such as splitting the sea, a staff becoming a serpent, or bringing the dead to life.

f: What opinion does the author reject regarding the nature of karāmāt?
b: He rejects the view that karāmāt cannot resemble prophetic miracles because they must differ from muʿjizāt. He argues that the distinction lies elsewhere, not in the type of miracle.

f: According to Saʿd al-Dīn al-Taftāzānī رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (quoting the Imām), what is the correct view regarding karāmāt?
b: All extraordinary events (khawāriq al-ʿādāt) are possible as karāmāt. They differ from prophetic miracles only because the saint does not claim prophethood.

f: What happens if a walī claims prophethood, according to al-Taftāzānī رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ?
b: He ceases to be a walī, becomes an enemy of Allah, deserves curse and humiliation rather than karāmah, and no longer merits divine honor.

f: How did Imām al-Nawawī view the claim that karāmāt cannot involve real transformations of created things?
b: He regarded that opinion as mistaken and contrary to observable reality, affirming that karāmāt may include genuine transformations of physical objects and similar extraordinary events.

f: Which scholars does the author cite as supporting the view that every type of supernatural event may occur as a karāmah?
b: He cites Saʿd al-Dīn al-Taftāzānī رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Imām al-Nawawī, Abū al-Barakāt al-Nasafī, and the commentator on al-Wahbāniyyah as affirming this view.

f: According to Imām al-Qushayrī, should a walī seek or become attached to karāmāt?
b: No. A walī should not become attached to, rely upon, or focus on the karāmāt that appear through him.

f: According to Imām al-Qushayrī, how do the awliyāʾ benefit from the appearance of karāmāt?
b: Their certainty and insight increase because they recognize that the karāmah is purely Allah's action, which strengthens their conviction in the truth of their beliefs.

f: According to Imām al-Qushayrī, what is the ruling on believing that karāmāt can appear through the awliyāʾ?
b: Believing that karāmāt may appear through the awliyāʾ is obligatory, and this is the position of the overwhelming majority of the people of spiritual knowledge (ahl al-maʿrifah).

f: Why does Imām al-Qushayrī say certainty regarding karāmāt is strong?
b: Because reports and accounts of karāmāt have been transmitted so abundantly in many different forms that they produce firm knowledge, leaving no room for reasonable doubt.

f: According to Imām al-Qushayrī, who develops certainty about the reality of karāmāt?
b: Anyone who associates with the people of the spiritual path and becomes familiar with their lives, reports, and experiences will no longer have any general doubt about the reality of karāmāt.

f: Which Qur'anic story does the author cite as evidence that awliyāʾ can perform karāmāt similar to prophetic miracles?
b: He cites the story of the man with knowledge from the Book in the court of Sulaymān عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, who said, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you" (Qur'an 27:40), referring to bringing the throne of Bilqīs instantaneously.

f: According to the author, who was the man who brought the throne of Bilqīs, and why is his story evidence for karāmāt?
b: He was Āṣif ibn Barkhiyā, whom the author regards as a walī rather than a prophet. His miraculous transportation of the throne demonstrates the possibility of karāmāt for the awliyāʾ.

f: Which incident involving ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ does the author cite as evidence for karāmāt?
b: He cites the authentic report that while delivering a Friday sermon, ʿUmar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ called out, "O Sāriyah, the mountain!" His voice reached Sāriyah at a distant battlefield, warning him of an ambush and enabling him to seek protection by the mountain.

f: How does the incident of "O Sāriyah, the mountain!" support the doctrine of karāmāt?
b: It demonstrates an extraordinary event in which Allah caused ʿUmar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ voice to reach a distant army, protecting them from the enemy, even though such transmission is beyond normal human ability.

f: Which events in the life of Maryam (Mary) does the author cite as evidence for karāmāt?
b: He cites Zakariyyā finding provision with her in the sanctuary, her reply, "It is from Allah" (Qur'an 3:37), and the fresh dates that fell from the palm tree outside their normal season (Qur'an 19:25).

f: Why does the story of Maryam support the doctrine of karāmāt according to the author?
b: Because Maryam was neither a prophet nor a messenger, yet Allah granted her extraordinary provisions and miracles, demonstrating that such events may occur for righteous non-prophets.

f: Which other Qur'anic stories does the author cite as evidence for karāmāt?
b: He cites the stories of the People of the Cave (Aṣḥāb al-Kahf), Dhū al-Qarnayn, and al-Khiḍr.

f: How does the story of the People of the Cave support belief in karāmāt?
b: The extraordinary events surrounding them—including their miraculous preservation and the wonders associated with them—demonstrate Allah's ability to grant supernatural favors to His righteous servants.

f: How does the story of Dhū al-Qarnayn support belief in karāmāt?
b: Allah granted him extraordinary power, dominion, and abilities beyond what was given to ordinary people, illustrating Allah's special favor upon certain righteous servants.

f: According to the author, what extraordinary acts of al-Khiḍr support the doctrine of karāmāt?
b: He cites al-Khiḍr's rebuilding of the collapsing wall, his hidden knowledge of divine wisdom unknown to Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, and other extraordinary acts that broke normal custom.

f: According to the author, was al-Khiḍr a prophet or a walī?
b: The author adopts the view that al-Khiḍr was a walī rather than a prophet, and that his extraordinary acts were karāmāt.

f: Besides Qur'anic evidence, what other evidence does the author mention for the reality of karāmāt?
b: He refers to numerous reports, narrations, and remarkable accounts from the Companions, the Tābiʿūn, and the recognized imams, stating that they are so numerous that a denier cannot realistically refute them.

f: Why does the author refrain from mentioning all the reports of karāmāt?
b: He says that recounting all of them would take him beyond the intended scope of the work.
